_readme: The coverage manifest. Every surface of the tree, where it is tested, and what is honestly not swept. `node tools/check-coverage.mjs` validates every claim in here against the tree on every gate run: files must exist, named tests must exist, and each invariant's pinning test must actually mention the thing it pins (the `keyword`). The mutation table doubles as the input to `node tools/mutation.mjs`, which breaks each guard and demands the pinning test fail. The narrative version of this file is docs/coverage.md; if the two ever disagree, the checker is right and the prose has rotted.

surfaces.note: 24 window test files, ~538 tests, run by `node test/run.mjs`

invariants.name: Near is a per-gap contract
invariants.why: M4: tantivy's slop is a summed budget, so the per-gap promise was recall loss. A mutation that tightens every step by one must be caught.

invariants.name: OCR structural rows are not words
invariants.why: tesseract's TSV carries level-1 and level-4 rows beside the words; if they leaked in, every page's words would be polluted.

invariants.name: Repairs attribute by time, not by key order
invariants.why: minor 17: a replay rebuilds the index through a key-sorted map; without the when-sort your repair attributes to whichever kind sorted last.

invariants.name: An anchor counts for the page it is on, and never a page before it
invariants.why: the boundary is what makes an anchor page its own page; a mutation to `<` unpages the anchor's own page and breaks the bijection between the pages a scan covers and the dafim they carry.

invariants.name: A small layer is never rewritten
invariants.why: M2: the floor is what keeps a store from rewriting the whole file for a stray deletion — and what keeps an unreadable file (0 lines, 0 live) from ever being rewritten at all.

invariants.name: A read-only MCP server refuses writes at the door
invariants.why: a client that remembered the tools from a writable session must be refused by name, not silently written into somebody's layer. The guard reads the crate's one list of writes, which is the point: the door and the catalogue cannot disagree about what writes.

invariants.name: A stored range is placed by its words and its Standing
invariants.why: A pin is the one placement in the links panel a reader vouched for, and it was placed by `SegmentId::covers` and by raw offsets — the two predicates this repository keeps two types for. A mutation that accepts any segment must be caught: `covers` says yes to a cut's child and to a se'if inserted beside it, and only the first is the parent's words. This is the only test that separates the two — through the panel they agree on every input it can produce, because an inserted se'if is not reachable by the link either.

invariants.name: A broken queue is not an empty queue
invariants.why: #55: `queue.lock().ok()?` made a poisoned queue answer as an empty one, every worker stood down, and `run` returned `Ok(0)` — which `girsa-fetch` prints as *complete* and exits 0 on. The comment above that line named the failure mode and the code could not express it, which is the audit's own finding. A mutation that restores the `None` must be caught.

invariants.name: A damaged index refuses rather than answering with less

test.keyword: a body row that will not parse is its own reason

invariants.why: #56 proposed skipping a row that will not parse. A row names the byte range the edges landing on one place live in, so skipping it makes the index answer with *fewer* edges than the gate — and it is the fast path, so nothing notices. That breaks the only property licensing a second read path: it may differ in speed and may not differ in answers. A mutation that skips instead of refusing must be caught, because this is the shape the proposal would have taken.

invariants.name: A citation resolves against the document it names
invariants.why: lamdan item 11: §9.4 is cited from the search crate, the ladder and the shell, and a renumbering is the one edit no compiler sees. The citation reads like a fact for exactly as long as nobody checks it, which is item 13 in the wild.

invariants.name: The shelf's steps are the program's, and the prose agrees in order
invariants.why: AUDIT-lamdan item 7: the order was written down in four places and the one that performs it is a program. This is the shape drift takes — a step swapped, dropped or added in the program while the docs keep saying *the six below* — and the pinning test reads the sequence out of this file, so a wrong order is a red gate rather than a shelf missing its fifth step.

invariants.name: A list that reaches the caches reaches the companions step
invariants.find: girsa-companions  corpus                     # which seforim open beside which
invariants.why: AUDIT-lamdan item 9 called `girsa-companions` the step easiest to miss, because nothing refuses without it: the מפרשים list is simply short, in a way a reader reads as *this sefer has no commentaries*. A documented list stopping before it is that failure written down, so deleting the line from the prose has to fail the test that names it — the first guard in this table whose source is a document and not code.

invariants.name: The lexicon the link importer needs is written by the import
invariants.why: #65: `girsa-link-import` refuses to start without `corpus/lexicon.tsv`, and that file used to come from an example nothing in a shelf build ran, so the documented one-command build died at step 3 on a fresh clone. The import now writes it out of the schemas it has already read, and this is the guard that keeps it written: delete the step and the test that names it goes red.

invariants.name: The OCR harness makes words the way the crate does
invariants.why: #12: the tree's one strict duplicate of Rust logic, and it cannot be deleted because the harness is node on a machine that may have no cargo. So the duplicate is pinned instead, and this is the pin's own guard: unfold the final forms and the harness starts comparing two ways of writing a mem, which turns a reported percentage into a smaller number that still looks like a percentage.

invariants.name: The writes are one list, and the catalogue is built from it
invariants.why: ten write tools were written out three times — the catalogue's second half, the door's alternation, the refusal test's table — so a tool added to one and not the others was a door that opened where the list said it was shut (#26). The difference between a writable catalogue and a read-only one now has to be exactly `WRITES`, which is a comparison and not a fourth copy.

invariants.name: The words as typed are an answer, and the ladder is not climbed
invariants.why: a near match offered as a source is the one failure this module is written around; `whole_word` is the asker saying *these words, not their near forms*, and turning it off silently would answer a different question than the one asked (#51).

invariants.name: A phrase search answers inside the scope it was given
invariants.why: a scope that is dropped on the way to the index is a *nothing in that sefer* answer to a question that was only asked about one sefer, and the count is the whole of the answer's honesty (#51).

invariants.name: A name nobody on the shelf is called is not matched to the nearest one
invariants.why: navigation that always resolves opens the wrong masechet with no sign it guessed; the bound is what makes `None` an answer (#63).

invariants.name: The worst word decides whether two names are one name
invariants.why: averaged, `bava batra` and `bava kamma` are 3/10 apart and the word that tells them apart is outvoted by the one they share (#63).

invariants.name: A sefer is not renamed by what follows its name
invariants.why: read from the back, `berakhot` is as close to `rashi on berakhot` as to `berakhot`, and the commentary ties with the masechet it comments on (#63).

uncovered.status: thin — the smallest crate in the tree and the least swept

platform_gated.what: the one thing in the gate that has ever seen a pixel
platform_gated.status: skipped on a machine with no browser — and the gate runs it with EYES_REQUIRED=1 so a skipped eyes is a red step, never a green one
platform_gated.requires: a browser (Edge on Windows, or EYES_BROWSER)

platform_gated.what: the engine probes, bounded but real
platform_gated.status: the engine's absence is pinned as a sentence, not a silence; the hung-probe bound is pinned; a real OCR run needs tesseract with heb installed

platform_gated.what: the window on the other two platforms
platform_gated.status: never seen — docs/not-yet.md is the honest account; the CI matrix builds and lints them, it does not look at them
platform_gated.requires: a Linux desktop with WebKitGTK, a Mac

platform_gated.surface: the semantic lane on a real shelf
platform_gated.status: the lane's coverage disclosure is pinned; an end-to-end embed needs the model and the two-library shelf
platform_gated.requires: the model weights and the shelf

platform_gated.what: the pen's side of the seam
platform_gated.status: CI checks out Ksav beside this tree and catches drift; a live pen is a machine this desk does not have
platform_gated.requires: Ksav's repository and a real pen
